subject: Monkey D. Luffy
gaps: All four supplied captures were read through their ends, including late ability sections, situational techniques, references, and navigation. Each is marked acquisitionTruncated=false. Images, linked pages, and underlying manga panels were not supplied for independent inspection.

No full main-character biography page was supplied. Identity is nevertheless directly supported by the substantive character-abilities subpage and both technique pages, not merely search hits or navigation lists. The Wano story page is corroborating arc evidence, not independently a character-resolution page.

The requested continuity is explicit, so no alternative-continuity assumption was necessary. The pages mix manga, anime, movies, games, and post-Wano material; only evidence attributable to the requested manga period is included as character capabilities.

Post-Wano Egghead and Elbaph feats are excluded, including encounters with Kizaru and the Elders, hearing Emet, Domi Reversi immunity, immortality inhibition, and purported later battles with Imu. Their presence in the supplied captures is not independent verification.

Later Gear 5 named techniques are excluded: Mogura Pistol, Dawn Whip, Dawn Rocket, Dawn Stamp, Dawn Gatling, Dawn Cymbal, Dawn Balloon, Dawn Pistol, Hara Senbei, the later Gear 5 Jet Gatling application, Majin, Suki Ari Bullet, Dawn Kraken Gatling, Dawn Thor Rifle, and Dawn Thor Bullet. The Wano predecessor of Star Gun is retained only as an unnamed attack.

Adaptation-only material is excluded, including anime-only Jet Lance, Jet Missile, Jet Rifle, Jet Axe and later anime-only attacks; game-only Red Hawk variants, Eagle Storm and Gigant Jet Gatling; Nightmare Luffy's game archery and fireballs; Afro Luffy's filler return; and Gear 5 Okaeshi, Uchiyaburu Kaishin no Ichigeki and Fist of Freedom. The manga Jet Spear and Hawk Rifle remain supported independently.

The supplied Gear 2 and Gear 5 navigation labels reverse or confuse the fruit's classification, and the Gear 5 overview calls Hito Hito no Mi its former name. For the Wano record, the substantive Wano revelation in the abilities page supports Gomu Gomu no Mi as the known name and Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika as the true Mythical Zoan identity.

The pages' broad imagination-to-reality wording cites supplementary Road To Laugh Tale material rather than supplying its full text. Arbitrary reality alteration, omnipotence, and unrestricted object creation are not established by the supplied Wano examples.

The Gear 5 discussion partly supports exhaustion, food restoration, temporary effects, and a general awakened-Zoan risk of personality takeover with post-Wano references. The latter risk and later recovery demonstrations are not imported into the Wano record; chapter-1045-linked lapse and heartbeat reactivation evidence is retained.

Localized Gear 4 use on isolated limbs and some general statements about post-awakening Gear mastery lack a clearly bounded Wano demonstration in these captures and are omitted. No separate Gear 3 or Gear 4 technique page was supplied, so their complete named arsenals and finer Tankman distinctions cannot be reconstructed.

The supplied pages mention many baseline techniques as comparison points, including Pistol, Stamp, Bazooka, Muchi, Bullet, Twin Pistol, Gatling, Rocket, Rifle, Yari, Ono, Ozuchi, Fusen, Kane, Elephant Gun, Elephant Gatling, and Over Kong Gun, but do not provide a complete baseline technique catalogue. Missing mechanics have not been filled from memory.

The pages directly support Seastone weakness and cutting vulnerability, but do not substantively explain swimming inability, the full effects of submersion, or all standard Devil Fruit weaknesses. The claim that inflation prevents sinking does not establish immunity to water; navigation links alone are insufficient to resolve the missing details.

Several statements are qualifications or in-world opinions rather than measured facts: Lucci's Gear 2 lifespan prediction, claims about Afro Luffy's power boost, and broad descriptions of poison immunity. Observed drawbacks and counterexamples are preserved instead of converting these into absolute powers.
Guidance is empty. No unsupported requested feature or unverified-memory claim has been added.

knowledge.subject: Monkey D. Luffy

identity.name: Monkey D. Luffy
identity.continuity: One Piece manga through the end of Wano Country arc
identity.explanation: The abilities page directly describes Monkey D. Luffy, captain of the Straw Hat Pirates, and both technique pages explicitly identify him as their user. Their manga-linked Wano material supports the requested continuity. The Wano story summary corroborates his Gear 5 victory over Kaidou, Emperor status, and 3-billion-berry bounty. Later manga developments and adaptation-only material are excluded.

claims.text: Luffy captains the Straw Hat Pirates, belongs to the Worst Generation, and seeks to become Pirate King. By Wano's conclusion, he has defeated Kaidou, become one of the Four Emperors, and received a bounty of 3,000,000,000 berries.

His defining combat style is creative, primarily unarmed fighting with a rubber body: stretching punches, kicks, and headbutts; twisting limbs for added force; inflating body parts; and combining these abilities with Haki and Gear techniques. He improvises counters during battle and uses terrain, opponents, and available objects opportunistically.

Luffy possesses exceptional strength, speed, agility, reflexes, durability, endurance, and willpower even apart from his Devil Fruit and Haki. His training includes Garp's harsh childhood exercises, two years on Rusukaina with instruction from Rayleigh, and strenuous prison labor while weakened by Seastone in Udon. He defeated a Pacifista with one punch after the timeskip and sustained battles against Cracker for 11 hours and Katakuri for over 9 hours.

His combat intuition includes finding Mr. 3 among duplicates by instinct, using random ricochets and an emptied mind against Enel's predictive Mantra, and discovering that water or his own blood lets him strike Crocodile's sand body. These are situational tactics rather than universal counters to prediction or intangibility.

Luffy has remarkable charisma and earns allies through loyalty, fearlessness, and helping friends. Seven crews totaling 5,640 people voluntarily pledged themselves as the Straw Hat Grand Fleet. The page also describes unusually fortunate survivals, including the lightning strike interrupting Buggy's execution attempt; it does not establish consciously controlled luck manipulation.

At age seven, Luffy ate the fruit known as the Gomu Gomu no Mi. Wano reveals its true identity as the Mythical Zoan Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika, associated with the liberating Sun God Nika. Its rubber physiology lets him stretch, bounce, bend, twist, and inflate his body.

His rubber body protects him from ordinary blunt impacts, can rebound bullets and cannonballs, and is immune to lightning. Inflation increases his ability to cushion and reflect impacts. Stretching and retracting his arms also lets him grab distant structures and propel himself toward them.

Rubber defenses do not make Luffy invulnerable: Armament Haki-enhanced blows can hurt him, and cutting attacks remain a weakness even in Gear 5. He has also been pierced by Katakuri's trident. Seastone handcuffs in Udon significantly weakened him and prevented use of his Devil Fruit powers, although he retained substantial physical strength.

After surviving Magellan's poisoning with Ivankov's treatment, Luffy developed resistance to many poisons, including Caesar's poisonous gases. This is not complete immunity: Armored Stonefish poison put him into a coma, and Queen's Mummy virus required Chopper's treatment despite Luffy initially claiming the ammunition would not work on him. Ivankov's lifesaving hormone treatment carried a lifespan cost.

Gear 2 accelerates circulation to deliver more oxygen and nutrients, greatly increasing speed and power; rubber blood vessels and organs withstand the pressure. Initially activated by pumping his legs, it can be activated through individual limbs after the timeskip and used in short, controlled bursts. Its manga debut is chapter 387.

Gear 2 consumes extra oxygen, nutrients, and energy, produces steaming sweat, and historically caused hunger, panting, declining performance, and severe post-use immobility. Lucci speculated that its bodily strain shortened Luffy's lifespan; no quantified loss is established here. Improved control reduces the drawbacks, and food replenishes depleted reserves.
Soru, translated as Shave, is disappearing-speed movement Luffy performs with Gear 2 after observing CP9. The technique page describes his execution as surpassing Blueno's.

Gomu Gomu no Jet Pistol is an extremely fast extended punch; Jet Stamp applies comparable speed to a forward sole-first kick; Jet Bullet is a powerful close-range punch; and Twin Jet Pistol strikes simultaneously with both clenched fists.

Gomu Gomu no Jet Bazooka is a high-speed double open-palm strike capable of breaking Blueno's strongest Tekkai guard. Jet Whip is a rapid sweeping kick. Jet Gatling is a barrage of nearly invisible punches, used to defeat Lucci; it can also be delivered in multiple directions while Luffy lies on his back, but its energy demands limit sustained use.

Gomu Gomu no Jet Rocket uses stretched arms gripping a target or object to launch Luffy forward at high speed. Jet Migawari, translated in the manga as Gum-Gum Human Shield Jet, rapidly pulls another person into an incoming attack's path; Luffy used Buggy against Mihawk.

Gomu Gomu no Gigant Jet Shell combines Gear 2 with Gear 3's Hone Fusen bone inflation, launching Luffy's enlarged body as a cannonball-like ram. It defeated Moria in Shadow's Asgard but originally combined Gear 2's exhausting strain with Gear 3's movement difficulty.

Post-timeskip Gear 2 techniques include Gomu Gomu no Jet Hammer, which wraps Luffy's legs around an opponent and rapidly slams them into the ground without the original hammer's twist-and-untwist motion; Jet Mace, a falling, spinning kick; and Jet Spear, a rapid version of his spear-like kick, used against the floor while fighting Monet.

Gomu Gomu no Red Hawk is a flaming, Armament-hardened Gear 2 punch. Luffy stretches his arm backward and strikes with an explosive fiery impact, demonstrated even underwater against Hody Jones. By the Onigashima battle, Kaidou chose to dodge it.

Gomu Gomu no Hawk Gatling is Armament-enhanced Jet Gatling, initially named Buso Koka: Gomu Gomu no Jet Gatling. Hawk Rifle adds Armament hardening to a twisting, spinning punch. Eagle Bazooka is the hardened double-arm version of Jet Bazooka.

Gomu Gomu no Hawk Whip is an elongated sweeping kick with the leg coated in Armament Haki. Hawk Stamp is an Armament-hardened extended sole strike, distinguished from the sweeping motion of Hawk Whip.

Gomu Gomu no Red Roc combines Elephant Gun's Gear 3 enlargement with Red Hawk, Gear 2, and advanced Armament Haki to deliver a huge flaming hardened punch that hurt Kaidou. Roc Gatling combines enlarged fists, Gear 2, Armament hardening, and Supreme King Haki infusion into a barrage capable of matching Kaidou's attacks.

Gear 3 enlarges particular body parts by blowing air into the bones through Luffy's thumb, producing giant-scale strikes capable of destroying steel doors and large buildings. Armament Haki and later Supreme King infusion increase its power. Before the timeskip it caused temporary child-sized shrinkage and impaired fighting afterward; the shrinkage no longer occurs after his two-year training.

Gear 4 was developed on Rusukaina and first displayed on Dressrosa. Luffy inflates his muscular structure and applies Armament Haki, producing distinct forms with different offensive and defensive priorities.

Gear 4 Boundman has a bouncing, rubber-ball-like body. Retracting limbs into the body and releasing them produces powerful blows; attacks can change direction, and the elastic, Haki-enhanced body rebounds many incoming attacks.
Gear 4 Tankman makes Luffy much bigger and emphasizes defense at the expense of speed. It weaponizes recoil by absorbing an opponent's attack and blasting the opponent away.
Gear 4 Snakeman is slimmer and emphasizes rapid, repeatedly redirecting attacks from many directions. It lacks the defensive capabilities of Boundman and Tankman.

Gear 4 overuses Haki and can leave Luffy weakened and unable to use Haki for ten minutes while it recharges. Repeated activation in a short period strains his body. During a recharge interval, even Gear 3 could not break Perospero's Candy Wall.

Gear 5 is the fruit's awakening, first attained during the climax of the Onigashima battle after Luffy's apparent death and defeat by Kaidou. It increases physical power, recovery, and freedom of bodily manipulation. His hair and clothing turn white, his eyebrows become billowing swirls, and a cloud-like collar surrounds him. His heartbeat takes the rhythm called the Drums of Liberation, and he becomes especially jubilant and playful.

In Gear 5, Luffy can change bodily shape and size without the usual air-pumping preparation, enlarge his entire body, and deform cartoonishly around incoming weapons. He can swing and slam Kaidou's dragon body and run through midair by rapidly spinning his legs. Malleability mitigates damage but does not eliminate pain or injury.

Gear 5 extends rubber properties into the environment, living targets, and lightning. Luffy used rubberized ground to cushion impacts and pull up a surface that reflected Kaidou's Bolo Breath. His strikes can stretch an opponent's body while still transferring damaging force.

The pages characterize the awakening as extraordinary freedom constrained by imagination and attribute broader 'imagination into reality' wording to Road To Laugh Tale. This is source interpretation, not evidence that Luffy is omnipotent or can produce arbitrary effects without limits.

Gear 5 is taxing and can lapse, leaving Luffy exhausted with an aged-looking appearance. The supplied page connects restarting his Drums of Liberation heartbeat to chapter 1045 and describes his ability to force continued fighting through willpower. No fixed Wano-era duration is established.

Gear 5 Gomu Gomu no Fusen, or Gum-Gum Balloon, makes Luffy exceptionally buoyant; he used it inside Kaidou. Gomu Gomu no Gigant, or Gum-Gum Giant, enlarges his entire body to giant size rather than enlarging only a limb.

Gomu Gomu no Dasshutsu Rocket, or Gum-Gum Escape Rocket, lets Luffy escape from inside Kaidou after Balloon by stretching his arms through Kaidou's eyes, grabbing his nose, and launching himself out. Gomu Gomu no Nawatobi, or Gum-Gum Jump Rope, uses Kaidou's dragon body as a skipping rope while Luffy is giant-sized.

Gomu Gomu no Kaminari, or Gum-Gum Lightning, rubberizes a lightning bolt so Luffy can grab it and throw it at his opponent. This is demonstrated against Kaidou; the supplied page distinguishes the anime's additional multiple-bolt use.

Gomu Gomu no Bajrang Gun enlarges Luffy's fist to almost Onigashima's size and combines advanced Armament emission with Supreme King Haki infusion. It is intended to strike without direct contact and is the finishing blow that defeats Kaidou. The page identifies it as a Gear 5 version of Over Kong Gun.

During the Wano fight, Luffy also delivers a spinning, enlarged, Haki-enhanced hook that deforms Kaidou's head. The Gear 5 page retrospectively associates this with Star Gun, but explicitly says that the attack was unnamed until a later fight; its later name is not treated as a Wano-era named technique.

Luffy can use all three types of Haki and their advanced applications by the end of Wano. Rayleigh taught him the basics during the timeskip; subsequent battles and Hyougoro's training further developed them.

Supreme King Haki can overwhelm weaker wills and knock out groups. Luffy learns selective targeting without harming bystanders, knocks out 50,000 opponents at Fish-Man Island, and even releases it while unconscious after Kaidou defeats him. The page identifies this type as his Haki specialty.

Advanced Supreme King Haki infuses Luffy's arms, legs, and body to greatly increase striking power, accompanied by black lightning. His initial control is described by Kaidou as crude and clumsy, but he subsequently clashes with Kaidou strongly enough to split the clouds overhead.

Observation Haki senses others' presence, emotions, and intent and assists anticipation and evasion. Luffy is particularly attuned to emotions. Fighting Katakuri unlocks short-term future sight; by Udon he can guide Hyougoro around attacks seconds before they occur and intercept Babanuki's Excite Shot before firing. Prediction is not automatic immunity to speed: Kaidou's Raimei Hakke still partially connects despite Luffy seeing ahead.

Armament Haki hardens Luffy's body, improves offense and defense, and lets him touch and damage Logia bodies and Katakuri's similar evasive physiology. It is integral to Gear 4 but can be depleted through overuse.

Advanced Armament emission projects Haki beyond Luffy's body; Internal Destruction sends it into a target to damage it from within. He first destroys his and Hyougoro's Death Collars in desperation, later consciously removes Yamato's explosive cuffs, and learns emission under Hyougoro. Against Kaidou, he judges advanced Armament damage alone 'too shallow' and supplements it with Supreme King infusion.

Atama Buso, or Head Armament, hardens Luffy's forehead in preparation for Gomu Gomu no Kane, a headbutt. Gear 2 Buso, or Gear Two Armament, hardens his fist during Gear 2 and prepares the ignition associated with Red Hawk. Armament: Koka denotes the hardening application illustrated on the abilities page.

Afro Luffy is the boxing outfit and afro worn against Foxy in the manga's Long Ring Long Land arc. Usopp and others claim that the afro increases power, but the page treats that claim as potentially joking or psychological rather than establishing a supernatural transformation.

Nightmare Luffy is an externally supplied, temporary enhancement created by infusing Luffy with 100 shadows separated by Moria's power. His strong spirit supports far more shadows than the usual two or three. He becomes much larger, blue-skinned, and grim in manner, while retaining rubber powers and gaining the shadows' combined strength and skills.

Nightmare Luffy can stop Oars' giant Rifle attack with one hand, deliver powerful blows, move fast enough to rescue Nami and Usopp unnoticed, and wield a sword through a swordsman's borrowed shadow skill. The form lasts only ten minutes, after which the shadows leave; its swordsmanship is not Luffy's normal proficiency.

Luffy generally lacks skill with conventional weapons. He used a metal pipe as a child, unsuccessfully attempted sword fighting and using Arlong's teeth, and carried Nidai Kitetsu mainly as a disguise prop in Wano.

Situational equipment includes Galdino's hard wax as hammer-like bindings and Champion Luffy armor, gloves, and boots, allowing protected contact with Magellan's poison. Enel's giant golden ball becomes a striking weapon in Gomu Gomu no Ogon Rifle. Mizu Luffy uses stored water and a barrel with a pump to counter Crocodile's sand body. These rely on externally available materials rather than intrinsic equipment creation.

Luffy's powerful jaws and enormous appetite have combat uses: biting through metal, destroying a dagger with his mouth, eating Cracker's Biscuit Soldiers with Nami's rain assistance, and escaping Katakuri's mochi by eating it. Large amounts of food and sleep help him rapidly recover from wounds and exhaustion; drinking milk restores a missing tooth.

The Voice of All Things lets Luffy hear Sea Kings and Zunesha. Hearing is not equivalent to command or fluent communication: Zunesha's voice overwhelms him, and unlike Momonosuke he cannot communicate with the elephant in the described encounter.

Noncombat shortcomings include reckless or poor decisions, very poor drawing ability, and inability to cook reliably: his attempted meal wasted a week's provisions and left the crew starving. Survival experience nevertheless gives him basic meat-roasting skills and limited knowledge of edible plants.
